name: R Draconis
description: Official test target. Mira variable (catalog period 245.6–247.2 d), 8.6° from the north ecliptic pole. Saturated in every exposure: measured offline in the PSF wings on all 2,493 SPHEREx exposures, it shows a 0.5–1.3 mag cycle of ~260 d in 2025–2026, in phase with AAVSO. The light curve below uses the wide survey only (539 exposures), so its period range (240–276 d) cannot tell ~260 d from the catalog value. Image brightness here is not a measurement.

notes: Automatic detection and catalog matching were not run.

Pixel values and stretch limits are IMAGE - ZODI (SPHEREx zodiacal model subtracted) in MJy/sr; PNGs use an asinh mapping with the same contrast for every frame of a detector, and transparent pixels mean no data. Saturated star cores that SPHEREx left empty (NaN) and detector-defect pixels (NONFUNC, HOT, COLD, PERSIST, SNOWBALL, and SUR_ERROR that is not part of a star's profile, e.g. cosmic-ray hits) are filled from their neighbours for display only; SUR_ERROR pixels on a star and finite OVERFLOW pixels are shown as recorded. All of them count as invalid in valid_fraction. thumb.png is a D2 frame.

Frame selection: downloaded 80 candidate frame(s) (up to 2 x max_frames=40) and kept 40, spread round-robin over seasons x detectors; inside each (season, detector) the frames whose wavelength at the field centre is closest to a per-detector reference (D1 0.898 um, D2 1.347 um, D3 2.145 um, D4 2.991 um, D5 4.089 um, D6 4.767 um) come first, then those nearest the season middle; frames without a known wavelength rank last. Rejected 0 bad frame(s) whose IMAGE - ZODI robust scatter exceeds 15x the noise of their VARIANCE plane (background steps) and 3x the median of the same detector's candidates (on bright nebulae every frame scatters more, so only outliers are rejected). Downloaded 104 more D2/D3 frame(s) only to find J/H/Ks wavelengths for the false-color composites; they are not blink frames.

Registration check: every frame's field stars were compared with their median position over the field's candidate frames (all detectors: a correct WCS puts a star at the same grid position at every wavelength); 55 of 80 blink candidate frame(s) and 77 of 104 J/H/Ks top-up frame(s) checked (kept: median 0.05 px, max 0.16 px); the other 52 had fewer than 3 field stars measurable to 0.15 px (e.g. around a saturated target) or too few frames for a consensus, and were kept unchecked.

False-color composites: 3 'detectors' and 1 'jhk' season composite(s) (infrared, not true color). detectors = full range: blue = D1 (fallback D2), green = D3 (D4), red = D6 (D5), coadds of the season's published frames. jhk = 2MASS-like: blue / green / red = coadd of the season's downloaded exposures (including unpublished candidates) within 0.06 µm of J 1.25 / H 1.65 / Ks 2.17 µm at the field centre, else the nearest one within 0.12 µm. Each channel: one weight per frame, sky removed, bad pixels left out; a pixel bad in every frame of a channel (saturated core, detector defect, ramp-fit error) is drawn neutral at the brightest channel's level, so saturated cores look white (display only). Green spans 2 sigma below the sky to the bright end of its usable pixels; red and blue are scaled to green by the median field-star flux ratio (target halo excluded), so typical bright field stars look white; limits shared by every season with the same detectors, except that a noisy channel (pixel noise above 3% of its range) has its black point set per season at its own sky + 2 sigma, so its speckle goes black (fainter field stars then look the complementary colour); colour-preserving asinh (Lupton et al. 2004). Skipped: detectors S2: no usable frame of D1 or D2 for blue; detectors S3: no usable frame of D1 or D2 for blue; jhk S1: no exposure within 0.12 µm of red (Ks 2.17 µm); nearest 2.406 µm; jhk S2: no exposure within 0.12 µm of blue (J 1.25 µm); nearest 1.633 µm; jhk S3: no exposure within 0.12 µm of blue (J 1.25 µm); nearest 1.645 µm; jhk S4: no exposure within 0.12 µm of red (Ks 2.17 µm); nearest 2.546 µm.

False color: SPHEREx infrared wavelengths mapped to red, green and blue (infrared, not true color).
Full range: red = D6 4.82 µm, green = D3 2.17 µm, blue = D1 0.97 µm (mean wavelength at the field centre).

Seasons use different detectors (red/green/blue = S0: D6/D3/D1; S1, S4: D5/D4/D1): colour differences between them can be instrumental (other wavelengths), so they are not evidence of a colour change of the object.

Colour balance: blue scaled to green by the median flux ratio of the field stars (blue x1.44; median of 1 season fit(s)), so typical field stars look white. Red could not be balanced (too few field stars); it uses its own limits.
Colours are relative to the field: typical bright field stars look roughly white and an object redder than they are looks red.
